AccountPatch.description:
`PATCH /accounts/{id}`: the owner names an account and says what kind it is (the assignment note and the tax
flags follow the type).
AccountPatch.title: AccountPatch

AdvanceIn.description:
Exactly one of `to`, `step` and `sync`. `to` at or before `revealed_through` answers an empty delta; `to` past
the window end is clamped and `at_end` is true. `step: "next_signal"` reveals through the next would-fire bar
close (a strategy-testing tool: it tells her a signal is coming); with none left it answers 422. `sync: true` is
the day-trade screen following the thread's server-side clock (ADR-0018): it brings a running clock to now, then
reveals this name through that clock, wherever it is; it moves nothing itself. `since` (with `sync` only) is the
playhead the caller last read: the answer carries what closed after it, so a second window on the same name, whose
session playhead the first window already moved, still gets every bar (D-198). Without it, the answer starts at
the session's own playhead.
AdvanceIn.title: AdvanceIn

AdvanceOut.description:
What the playhead revealed in `(previous, revealed_through]`: display-interval bars that closed inside
it, the forming bar, the prints (size-filtered, capped), the would-fire signals whose bar closed inside it,
and the levels, last print and open trade at the new playhead.
AdvanceOut.title: AdvanceOut

CandidateLiveOut.description:
A listed name as of the day clock `at`, from bars closed by it. `price`: the last closed 1-minute bar of the day
(null before the first); `change_pct`: its move from the prior close; `metrics`: the metric block cut at the clock,
which is today's when `today` and the previous session's while no regular-session bar has closed.
CandidateLiveOut.title: CandidateLiveOut

CandidateOut.description: One name on the list, as of `data_through`. `list_price` is the price at the evaluating filter's cut.
CandidateOut.title: CandidateOut

ClockAccountOut.description:
The simulated account at the clock: the ledger's `balance` (realized), what every open position is worth over its
cost at the clock (`open_pnl_usd`), and `equity_usd`, the two together; `since_start_usd` is equity less the
starting balance. `buying_power_usd` is the cash an entry can use: the balance less the cost of the open
positions and the cash its working orders hold back, the figure the order check enforces. Every position is
marked by one function at the clock, never past it.
ClockAccountOut.title: ClockAccountOut

ClockIn.description:
Play or pause (`running`), the speed, and a step or jump (`step` one bar; `to` a date and time with its UTC
offset, no later than `horizon`). Any mix, at least one; a step or jump is forward only (a `to` in the past is a
422).
ClockIn.title: ClockIn

CoveredCallCandidateOut.description:
The engine's `core.covered_calls.Candidate`, flattened. Yields are fractions (0.16 = 16%); `spread_pct` is a
percentage of the mid.
CoveredCallCandidateOut.title: CoveredCallCandidateOut

CurvePointOut.description: A point of the balance curve: `n` 0 is the starting balance (no date), then one per date with a trade.
CurvePointOut.title: CurvePointOut

DailyBlockOut.description:
The Daily chart: the rebased bars through the session before the day (never the day's own), the forming candle
built from revealed one-minute bars, and this name's open hold for the entry marker and the stop line.
DailyBlockOut.title: DailyBlockOut

EarningsChipOut.description: An explicit report date and timing within the next ten sessions. Never a guess from a gap (02p a3 rule 9).
EarningsChipOut.title: EarningsChipOut

FeedOut.title: FeedOut

FeedbackCountsOut.description: Reports per status over the whole log, not over the page.
FeedbackCountsOut.title: FeedbackCountsOut

FeedbackCreateIn.description:
File a report. A bug carries a severity and a feature request does not; `attachment_ids` are screenshots the
caller staged earlier (`POST /attachments`).
FeedbackCreateIn.title: FeedbackCreateIn

FeedbackItemOut.description: A row of the dashboard list.
FeedbackItemOut.title: FeedbackItemOut

FeedbackPatchIn.description:
Either a status change (the owner: `status`, `fix_ref`, `duplicate_of`, `note`) or the filer's own edit while the
report is open (`title`, `body`, `expected`, `severity`, `links`); a key left out is left alone.
FeedbackPatchIn.title: FeedbackPatchIn

FillOut.description:
One execution of a thread: a Buy or a Sell with its shares, price and time. `closes` of the shares closed the
name's position and `opens` opened or added to one (a flip has both). `day` is the data day its lane opened on.
FillOut.title: FillOut

FormingBarOut.description: The current display bar built from revealed closed 1-minute bars; it updates once a minute.
FormingBarOut.title: FormingBarOut

FundamentalAlertPut.description:
`PUT /fundamental-alerts/{template}`: whatever is sent changes, the rest stays; a change saves a new strategy
version.
FundamentalAlertPut.title: FundamentalAlertPut

Fundamentals.description:
02n §c4: the metric keys a holdings row, a `long_term` watchlist row and the `Columns` menu share. Numbers or
null, never NaN; a date or a rating where the key says so.
Fundamentals.title: Fundamentals

HoldOut.description:
A practice hold as the screens read it. Days are numbers and weekdays, never dates. An open hold carries
`unrealized_usd`, a closed one `pnl_usd`; `price_basis` says which price an open one is valued at.
HoldOut.title: HoldOut

IndicatorRowOut.description:
The indicators of one bar (`t` is its open), computed on the server from the same cut as the bars, the price and
the forming candle. A value that has not warmed up is null, never filled.
IndicatorRowOut.title: IndicatorRowOut

IndicatorsOut.description:
`rows` are the indicators of the bars this payload carries (an advance: the new bars; a feed: every returned bar)
and then of the forming candle, whose close is the price. `as_of_bar` is the open of the last bar included.
IndicatorsOut.title: IndicatorsOut

JournalOut.description:
Live while the session is active (realized plus the open trade marked at the playhead); final after
`end`. `signals_vs_trades` and the 15/30-minute changes look past the playhead, so they are empty until
the session has ended.
JournalOut.title: JournalOut

LaneBriefOut.description: A name in the thread's book: a row of the Screen's lanes. Flat unless `position` is set.
LaneBriefOut.title: LaneBriefOut

LibraryExampleOut.description: A real occurrence on stored bars (the stub's snapshot here); the mock draws it as an example.
LibraryExampleOut.title: LibraryExampleOut

LibraryItemOut.description: One catalog entry, as `PresetCatalogV1` ships it, plus whether it can be attached.
LibraryItemOut.title: LibraryItemOut

ListUniverseOut.description: What was scanned. `label` and `footnote` state the universe plainly; show them beside any score.
ListUniverseOut.title: ListUniverseOut

MarketOut.description:
The exchange's state at the thread time (a day thread's payloads): `phase`, when the day's tape ends, when the
last bar of the name closed (null where the payload names no single name), and when the next trading day's data
starts (null on the plan's last day). After `tape_end` the day has no bars: nothing is filled across the gap.
MarketOut.title: MarketOut

Metrics.description: The snapshot's metric names, exactly (02m §a1). Numbers or null, never NaN.
Metrics.title: Metrics

OpenTradeOut.description:
The name's open position: shares and `entry_price`, their average cost, however many fills built it. For a swing
session it is the name's practice hold (`trade_no` is the hold id) and the four last fields say how long it has been
held and which price it is valued at; a day session leaves them out.
OpenTradeOut.title: OpenTradeOut

OrderOut.description:
A practice order that was not filled at once, and what became of it (the fill rules are in the orders module).
A fill is also an entry mark (`mark_id`).
OrderOut.title: OrderOut

PaceOut.description: Eligible prints and shares per market second over the last `window_s` seconds before the playhead.
PaceOut.title: PaceOut

PausedOut.description:
A stop was crossed: the playhead stopped at the close of the first one-minute bar that did (02p b5). It is a
pause, never an exit. `also` lists every other hold crossed in the same minute.
PausedOut.title: PausedOut

PeekOut.description:
Pre-open chart data for one candidate, cut at `data_through`: the same rebased daily bars the list was
screened on, and the day's minutes through the cut.
PeekOut.title: PeekOut

PortfolioOut.description:
`GET /threads/{id}/portfolio`: every open position across the thread's lanes at its time, the working orders and
the account. Jump a month ahead and the first read prices every holding at the new time.
PortfolioOut.title: PortfolioOut

PortfolioPositionOut.description:
An open position at the thread's time: its average cost, its price AT THAT TIME (`mark_at`, never the cost
unless the name has no price at all: then `price_at` is null), the gain or loss, and how long it has been held.
PortfolioPositionOut.title: PortfolioPositionOut

PracticePlanOut.description:
The thread's saved plan: a `PracticeSetupV2` (a plan saved before ADR-0025 is a `PracticeBlockV1`, served as it
was stored without its legacy plan fields) and her filters by name.
PracticePlanOut.title: PracticePlanOut

ProviderOptionOut.description:
One provider's standing in one class. `state` is the bridge's own health state; `detail` is its
reason code (never rendered raw -- the card maps both to words, 02t §6).
ProviderOptionOut.title: ProviderOptionOut

ReplaySessionPatch.description: PATCH body: notes and the self-rating only.
ReplaySessionPatch.title: ReplaySessionPatch

RescanJobOut.description:
A re-scan's progress, for the screen to poll while `state` is `running`: `done` of `total` symbols read
(`total` is 0 until the job has counted them), at the day clock `as_of`. `failed` carries a plain `message`.
RescanJobOut.title: RescanJobOut

RescanOut.description:
The latest re-scan of the day's filters (02o-b2), run at the day clock `as_of` on data through `data_through`.
Its names ARE the day list above (the scan repopulated it); this is the label: which scan, the clock it ran at, the
time its data stops, and how many names it added. `seq` counts the day's scans.
RescanOut.title: RescanOut

ScreenOut.description:
The thread's Screen (ADR-0025): her filters evaluated at the thread's time `as_of`, her stars, and the names she
holds. Nothing here is later than `data_through` (the list, the stars, Peek) or the clock.
ScreenOut.title: ScreenOut

ScreenPatch.description:
PATCH body: the stars (at most 20 names from the Screen), notes, and the self-rating. A key left out is left
alone; `null` clears notes and rating.
ScreenPatch.title: ScreenPatch

SettingsChannelStateOut.description:
`locked` is true only for the inbox, and `configured` is false until the owner wires the
channel's key. The inbox row is sent without `configured`, and telegram/slack without `locked`
(the endpoint uses `response_model_exclude_unset`), which is the a3.8 example shape.
SettingsChannelStateOut.title: SettingsChannelStateOut

Stamp.description: Embedded in every response that carries market data; the UI never computes freshness.
Stamp.title: Stamp

StripRowOut.description:
A row of the day strip: every open hold, then the focus names, at most ten. `last` is the last revealed regular
session price at the DAY CLOCK; `chg_pct` is against the restated prior close.
StripRowOut.title: StripRowOut

ThreadBriefOut.description:
The header strip of a workspace: the SIMULATED balance (the ledger: realized P/L only; an open position is valued
by the Portfolio and the clock's account).
ThreadBriefOut.title: ThreadBriefOut

ThreadCapacityOut.description:
The thread slots, shared by every user: at most `day_max` active threads at once. Closing a thread frees a slot.
The field names keep their contract names until the contract migration.
ThreadCapacityOut.title: ThreadCapacityOut

ThreadClockBriefOut.description: Where the thread's time is, for a row of the hub's list (the clock route has the account and the market).
ThreadClockBriefOut.title: ThreadClockBriefOut

ThreadClockOut.description:
The freestyle thread's clock (ADR-0025, ADR-0018): real time, shifted. `clock` is the simulated time at
`server_now` (a running clock was settled before this was built); a client may extrapolate it with `speed` between
polls but never owns it. It runs through the close, the night and the weekend: nothing happens at them. `horizon`
is the latest time it can reach (the extended close of the latest session available under the 15-minute embargo): a
running clock stops there with `pause = {"kind": "horizon"}`. `next_open` is the first regular open after `clock`
(the Next open preset), null past the horizon.
ThreadClockOut.title: ThreadClockOut

ThreadDateOut.description:
One ET date that realized a trade, in date order: a grouping key for the journal, nothing more. `balance` is the
SIMULATED balance after that date's trades.
ThreadDateOut.title: ThreadDateOut

ThreadFillsOut.description: The newest executions of a thread, newest booking first. `total` counts every one.
ThreadFillsOut.title: ThreadFillsOut

ThreadLedgerOut.description: The newest ledger rows, newest first. `total` counts every row.
ThreadLedgerOut.title: ThreadLedgerOut

ThreadSummaryOut.description:
A thread with its plan and stats (the contract), its clock and how many positions it holds. A row of the hub's
"Your threads" list. `clock` is null before the thread's plan starts it.
ThreadSummaryOut.title: ThreadSummaryOut

UniverseDayOut.description: One morning's recorded membership. `recorded` false: no pass wrote it, so that day's list scans today's set.
UniverseDayOut.title: UniverseDayOut

UniverseDaysOut.description:
The `universe_days` read path: its coverage, the first day a new plan should default to (null until 20 finished
days have been recorded), and with `?day=` that morning's membership.
UniverseDaysOut.title: UniverseDaysOut

UniverseMembershipOut.description:
Where the scanned names came from (02o-b2): the symbols the Desk recorded for that morning (`universe_days`), or
today's Desk set for a day before the recording began. `note` says so in plain words.
UniverseMembershipOut.title: UniverseMembershipOut

WatchCheckOut.description:
"Traded only names on your watch": data for the screen to render. `traded` is the names she entered a trade on;
`off_watch` the ones she had not starred. Nothing scores it.
WatchCheckOut.title: WatchCheckOut

WatchlistOrder.description: `PUT /api/desk/watchlists/{id}/order`: the list's own symbols in their new order.
WatchlistOrder.title: WatchlistOrder

WatchlistTableRow.description:
`fundamentals` is a `long_term` list's (02n §c3 #20): a row of an intraday or swing list leaves it out, so those
responses are byte for byte what they were (`SwingOptional`'s rule, whatever the lane).
WatchlistTableRow.title: WatchlistTableRow

patch.description: Name an account and say what kind it is.

Response List Alert Strategy Fires Api Desk Alert Strategies  Strategy Id  Fires Get
Response List Alerts Api Desk Alerts Get
Response Delivery Log Api Desk Alerts Log Get

get.description:
Closed bars for the chart. `ext` marks pre/after-hours bars; `stamp` is the freshness the UI shows.
Stub (`DESK_MVP_STUB=1`): SPY, NVDA, MSFT from the snapshot, `session=extended` reads the Friday 5m series.

Pattern markers on closed bars (drawn below the bar) plus the fires of her strategies (a bell above),
filtered to `from`..`to` on the bar start for patterns and the bar time for fires.

The engine's top three calls for one holding, from the delayed spot and chain read now; an empty list with an
unavailable chain stamp when the chain cannot be read.
Coverable contracts per holding and account, with the reason in words.

schema.title: Response Short Calls Api Desk Covered Calls Short Calls Get

get.description: Cost to close, roll candidates and the assignment note for one open short call.

The Fundamental Today screen's one aggregate read (02n §c3 #1). Contract-first: `DESK_FUNDAMENTAL_STUB=1` answers
from the invented world, otherwise 503 until the real service lands.

The dashboard: reports newest first by default, and the counts per status over the whole log. `limit` guards the
answer; the Desk shows one scrolling list.

post.description: File a bug or a feature request. The screenshots are the caller's own staged files, named by id.

Stage a screenshot before the report exists, so the form can show the upload before Send. Staged files older
than 24 hours are deleted by this route on its next call; a user holds at most six.

delete.description: Remove one of the caller's own staged screenshots (the form's Remove). A file already on a report stays: 409.

get.description: The bytes. A staged file is its uploader's alone; an attached one is every signed-in user's.

200.description: The screenshot's bytes, with the stored content type.

patch.description:
The owner moves a report between statuses (`status`, with `fix_ref`, `duplicate_of` or `note` where the status
needs them); the filer edits her own report while it is open. One request does one of the two.

post.description: Add a screenshot to an existing report: the filer or the owner, up to six in all.

schema.title: Response List Alerts Api Desk Fundamental Alerts Get

get.description:
ES, NQ, CL and GC rows (front contract, last, week range, roll, expiry) and the week's macro releases (02n
§c3 #11). Contract-first: `DESK_FUNDAMENTAL_STUB=1` answers from the invented world, otherwise 503 until the real
service lands.

schema.title: Response Futures Specs Api Desk Futures Specs Get

get.description: Import state, accounts, totals, one row per held symbol and the option lots.

post.description:
Start the Flex import and answer 202 with the running state; the statement is fetched and stored in the
background (idempotent per account and statement date). Only the Desk user named by `DESK_FLEX_USER` may start
it.

404.description: The import belongs to another Desk user

409.description: An import ran in the last 60 seconds (Flex allows 10 requests a minute)

503.description: The Flex import is not set up

get.description: The tax lots and the open short calls of one symbol.

schema.title: Response List Library Api Desk Library Get

get.description:
Server-sent events, one connection per symbol. Each `quote` event's data is JSON:
`{"symbol", "close", "quality", "as_of", "freshness", "source", "session"}`.
`as_of` is the closed 1m bar's start (`+00:00`, `Z` in the stub).
`freshness` is live|delayed|closed|paused|unavailable; `source` is the bar's provider;
`session` is pre|regular|after|closed (the market session now).
An event is sent only when the quote changes; the stream stays open until the client disconnects.
Stub: one event for SPY, NVDA or MSFT from the last 15m fixture bar, then the stream stays open.

patch.description: Notes and the self-rating only; a key left out is left alone, `null` clears it.

post.description:
Follow the thread's clock (`sync`): the only thing a name may do to time. `to` and `step` are a 422 (a name does
not move the thread's time; the thread's clock does, forward only).
Place a practice mark at the playhead: the server stamps the time and the last print's price.

delete.description: Undo the last mark, only while the playhead has not moved since it was placed (else 409).

post.description:
Place a limit, stop or stop-limit practice order, GTC (default) or Day (`timeInForce`). It fills when the
thread's clock crosses a later one-minute bar that proves it, however many days that takes (or at once at the last
print when a limit already accepts it); a market entry is a mark. A closing order is derived reduce-only.

delete.description: Cancel a working practice order (409 once it has filled or been cancelled).

get.description: Her threads, the active ones first, each with its plan, stats and today (the hub's resume list).

schema.title: Response List Threads Api Desk Replay Threads Get

post.description:
Start a freestyle practice thread from a `PracticeThreadCreateV1`: a SIMULATED starting balance (default 50,000)
and the risk plan. A `setup` key beside them (a `PracticeSetupV2`: the start instant, her filters, the chart setup)
also starts the thread's clock, paused at `startAt`, and its Screen. `mode: swing` is closed (409, ADR-0025).
Threads share ten slots across all users (a full house is a 409 on `mode`; closing a thread frees a slot). Each
thread has its own balance and its own `name` (the server gives it one: "Freestyle · Oct 15", "(2)" when she
already has it).

schema.description: A PracticeThreadCreateV1, plus an optional `setup` (a PracticeSetupV2)

get.description:
The day-trade slots in use across all users and the most there can be (10). Declared before
`/threads/{thread_id}`, which would otherwise read "capacity" as an id.

delete.description:
Delete the thread and everything under it: its ledger, plans, Screen and lanes. It cannot be undone; a thread
that is not hers is a 404.

get.description:
One thread: its plan, stats, today, the daily P/L series (one row per ended day) and the balance curve. Every
figure is read back from the ledger; nothing is stored twice.

patch.description:
Replace the risk plan and the entry size (`shares`, a day thread only; left out clears it) while the thread is
active (a closed thread is a 409). It applies from the next session: a session already started keeps the plan and
the size it began with.

get.description:
The thread's clock now (ADR-0025): its state, speed, the simulated time, when the first regular open after it
is (`next_open`), the latest time it can be jumped to (`horizon`) and the simulated account at that time (balance,
open P/L, equity). A running clock is brought to now first, so this is the answer whether or not anyone was
looking in between. Nothing happens at a close or an open. Poll it; it is idempotent.

post.description:
Play or pause the thread's clock, set its speed (1, 2, 5, 10), step it a bar, or jump it:
`{"to": "<ISO time with its UTC offset>"}` sets the clock to that date and time (Next open is a Jump to
`next_open`).
Forward only (422 on a `to` already past; a `to` equal to the clock changes nothing) and no later than `horizon`
(422). Every position and working order is kept: orders fill as the clock crosses them, splits restate holdings, and
each position is valued at the new time. A running clock stops at the horizon with `pause`.

Close the thread (ADR-0025 P1): its working orders are cancelled ("Thread closed"), its plan is archived and its
clock freezes where it is. Every position stays open, valued at the frozen time; nothing is sold or booked.
Idempotent.

get.description:
The thread's executions (ADR-0018), newest first: every Buy and Sell with its shares, price and time, and how
many of the shares closed the name's position. The server keeps the book; the screen never rebuilds a trade from
memory.

post.description:
Open her lane on a name (or resume it): one book per name for the thread's life, at the thread's time. Any name
of the Screen or of the thread's universe opens, and a position open on another name never blocks the switch.

get.description: The thread's realized practice trades (`PracticeLedgerEntryV1`), newest first: the rows its balance is of.

The thread's Portfolio at its time T (ADR-0025): every open position across its lanes with its average cost, its
price AT T (the one price function, `mark_at`) and its gain or loss, the working orders, and the account. Jump a
month ahead and the first read prices every holding at the new time.

The thread's Screen (ADR-0025): the latest scan of her filters at the thread's time, her stars, the names she
holds, and (with `peek`) the pre-open chart data of one candidate. With `live`, each candidate also carries `live`:
the name priced at the thread's time (nothing later); the scan's values stay in the candidate itself.

patch.description: Stars (at most 20 names from the Screen, each stamped with the thread's time), notes and the self-rating.

post.description:
Start a re-scan of the Screen's filters at the thread's time (02o-b2) and answer at once: the Screen with
`rescan_job` `running` and its `done` of `total` symbols read. Poll `GET /threads/{id}/screen` while it runs. When
`state` is `done` the scan has REPOPULATED the Screen (its names, columns and counts are the scan's) and `rescan`
labels it with the time it ran at. Stars and lanes stay; a name she holds or starred that the scan no longer matches
stays on the Screen as `held_over`. A scan already running is joined, not doubled; a second scan at the same time
starts nothing. A 409 on a closed thread and for a filter that cannot have bars at this time yet.

put.description:
Save the thread's setup (a `PracticeSetupV2`): the start instant, her filters and the chart setup. The first one
starts the thread's clock, paused at `startAt`; a later one replaces the plan and the Screen's filters and never
moves time. A closed thread is a 409.

get.description:
The recorded universe (02o-b2): which mornings the Desk recorded the names it scanned, the first day a new plan
defaults to once 20 finished days are recorded, and with `day` that morning's membership. A day without a recording
scans today's Desk set, and says so.

Every analyzed stock after the close, the run summary and the track-record counts. No Desk AI run exists before
step 5: no rows, no run, and the track record counts the stored calls.
Consensus EPS, revisions and analyst targets from the stored snapshots; `verdict` is null until step 5.
The four valuation methods per share, the 60/40 blend against the price, and the earnings reaction.

schema.title: Response List Filters Api Desk Screener Filters Get

get.description:
The filter's newest stored run. Before its first run it answers 200 with no matches and an
`unavailable` stamp (no `as_of`), so the screen can say "Waiting for the first scan" without an error.

post.description:
Evaluate an unsaved spec over the stored universe, never a provider, within `PREVIEW_BUDGET_SECONDS`.
Over budget it answers `matches_total: null` and no `top` (a partial ranking would mislead).

get.description:
The desk's technical view for one timeframe. Stub (`DESK_MVP_STUB=1`): SPY, NVDA, MSFT from the snapshot;
`gauges.strategies` is a sample for NVDA 15m only. Real mode computes everything from the bars: the last
values (`indicators`), the bias history and its newest change, the key `levels`, and the fourth gauge from
her strategies (null with none on this timeframe).
